checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is rate-limiting per-peer implemented to prevent sidecar request flooding from exhausting validator resources?

reachability.notes: The MUST-serve requirement for sidecars creates a protocol-level amplification vector. Without rate-limiting, an attacker can exhaust validator resources.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all P2P entry points where sidecar requests (DataColumnSidecarsByRoot, DataColumnSidecarsByRange) are received. 2. Review the request handler implementation for the presence of per-peer rate-limiting logic. 3. Verify that rate limits are enforced before processing requests, not after resource allocation. 4. Attempt to flood the validator with sidecar requests from a single peer and measure resource consumption (CPU, memory, I/O). 5. Verify the validator continues to perform consensus duties (attestations, proposals) under request flood conditions. 6. Check that rate-limited peers receive appropriate error responses (ResourceUnavailable or similar). 7. Confirm rate-limiting state is tracked per-peer and cannot be bypassed via peer identity rotation.

checklist.title: Verify Resource Isolation: Does sidecar request processing have bounded resource allocation that cannot starve consensus duties?

reachability.notes: Resource isolation between P2P request handling and consensus duties is critical to prevent DoS-induced validator penalties.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the threading/goroutine model for sidecar request handling. 2. Verify that sidecar request processing uses a separate, bounded worker pool from consensus processing. 3. Check for resource limits (max concurrent requests, memory caps, I/O throttling) on sidecar serving. 4. Simulate high sidecar request load while the validator is scheduled to produce a block or attestation. 5. Verify that consensus duties complete within timing constraints even under maximum sidecar request load. 6. Check that sidecar request timeouts/cancellations do not leak resources. 7. Review disk I/O prioritization to ensure sidecar reads cannot starve beacon state reads.

checklist.title: Verify Rate Limit Enforcement: Can rate limits be bypassed through protocol-level manipulation or peer spoofing?

reachability.notes: Rate-limiting is only effective if peer identity is reliably tracked and limits cannot be reset.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review peer identification mechanism used for rate-limiting (libp2p peer ID, IP address, or both). 2. Test whether disconnecting and reconnecting resets rate limits for a peer. 3. Test whether multiple peer IDs from the same IP can bypass rate limits. 4. Check for time-based rate limit reset vulnerabilities (e.g., can an attacker burst, wait, burst again?). 5. Verify rate limits apply to both DataColumnSidecarsByRoot and DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests. 6. Test whether malformed requests that fail early still count toward rate limits. 7. Check for race conditions in rate limit counter updates under concurrent requests.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can an adversary infer validator custody group membership by probing column response behavior?

reachability.notes: An adversary can systematically request all columns from a validator and measure response times or availability to infer custody assignments.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P request handler for data column requests (tb-012 boundary). 2. Analyze response timing for custody vs non-custody columns by measuring latency distributions. 3. Check if there are observable differences in availability patterns (e.g., faster responses for cached custody columns vs fetched non-custody columns). 4. Verify that the implementation does not leak custody status through error messages or response codes. 5. Test for timing side-channels by sending bursts of requests for all columns and correlating response times with known custody assignments. 6. Validate that rate-limiting and response delays are uniform across all column types.

checklist.title: Verify Timing Uniformity: Are response times for custody columns indistinguishable from non-custody columns?

reachability.notes: Timing side-channels can reveal custody assignments even when availability appears uniform.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Instrument the validator node to log precise timing of DataColumnSidecar request handling. 2. For a validator with known custody group assignments, send requests for: (a) custody columns the validator MUST store, and (b) non-custody columns the validator MAY store opportunistically. 3. Collect timing samples (N > 1000) for each column type under identical network conditions. 4. Perform statistical analysis (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, t-test) to determine if timing distributions are distinguishable. 5. If p-value < 0.05, timing side-channel exists - document the observable difference and its exploitability. 6. Check if caching behavior differs between custody and non-custody columns, creating observable timing patterns. 7. Measure variance in response times - higher variance for non-custody columns could also be a distinguishing factor.

checklist.title: Verify Availability Uniformity: Does column availability status reveal custody group membership?

reachability.notes: If validators only serve custody columns reliably, availability patterns directly reveal custody assignments.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. For a target validator, enumerate all 128 data columns and track which columns the validator serves during the retention period (SG-007). 2. Compare the served columns against the expected custody group for that validator's node_id and epoch. 3. Verify that validators serve columns beyond their strict custody requirement (either all columns or a randomized superset). 4. Check if 'column not available' responses correlate with non-custody columns. 5. Test across epoch boundaries to see if availability patterns shift predictably with custody reassignments. 6. Document any correlation between served columns and custody assignments that could be used for fingerprinting. 7. Check if partial availability (serving some non-custody columns but not others) creates a distinguishable pattern.

checklist.title: Verify Anti-Fingerprinting Countermeasures: Are there mitigations against custody inference attacks?

reachability.notes: The SHOULD NOT requirement indicates recommended protections that may not be universally implemented.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the validator implementation for countermeasures such as: (a) Opportunistic storage of non-custody columns to normalize availability, (b) Artificial delay injection to normalize response times, (c) Random response ordering for batch requests, (d) Consistent error handling regardless of custody status. 2. If countermeasures exist, test their effectiveness by repeating timing and availability analysis (CHK-0005, CHK-0006). 3. If no countermeasures exist, document this as a potential vulnerability requiring client-specific analysis. 4. Assess the computational and storage overhead of implementing full-column storage as a privacy countermeasure. 5. Verify that any randomization in countermeasures uses cryptographically secure random number generation to prevent predictability attacks.
